answer: A report should weigh only as much as its author's earlier forecasts proved right, so a newborn name speaks at zero volume. Agents counting snowy owls, pale as ivory, on the tundra each predict the next dawn tally before it is taken. A rival who spawns three hundred names to inflate a count is outvoted by one veteran whose past numbers held, and his crowd stays weightless until a season of its own guesses comes true.
